note: Four of five criteria met cleanly. He owns a real estate investment business with three closings this month, said outright 'The price is not a problem' and had anchored himself at $15,000, and he framed health as the single remaining unfixed area of an otherwise sorted life — 'this is the last thing in my life that I need to fix right now, I fixed everything else, except this', which is almost a verbatim restatement of the neglected-health criterion. He is emphatically not gym-averse or deconditioned either: he presses double 50 lb kettlebells and is an ex-MMA fighter. The one miss is starting point, and it is material — at 236 lb against a 205 lb fighting weight he described himself as 'very overweight' and 'just like a boulder right now'. That is rescue, not good to great. The finding worth carrying up: on 12 June the sales manager described the actual target as men in their 40s and 50s who 'have life together, they might have some injuries' and 'need to lose maybe 20, 30, 40 pounds'. Jay Moreno is the exact centre of that description and the single criterion he fails is the one the company has already privately abandoned. He should be read as evidence that the stated ICP, not the prospect, is the thing out of date.
